a1mini.notes: No official A1 mini CAD exists (confirmed by the Printables author's note and forum). Only downloadable body CAD is the low-fidelity Printables STEP (NOT to scale: 219 x 272 x 346 mm bbox vs real 347 x 315 x 365), so build a parametric model from the official numbers: 347 W x 315 D x 365 H printer; 358 mm wide front envelope incl. X-motor/camera box; Z column on the RIGHT (viewed from front) toward the rear; bed-slinger with ~184 x 197 mm plate sweeping a 390 mm Y envelope; internal PSU (no brick); spool holder hangs off the REAR face of the Z column (depth ~485 mm with spool, community). AMS lite 397 x 208 x 342 mm stands 50 mm to the right of the printer (612 mm total width, 483 mm total height). Printables files were fetched through the site's public GraphQL download-link API from the runner because the HTML page is Cloudflare-challenged.

piper.notes: Full-arm STEP obtained (AIFITLAB Shopify CDN = same store as the known gripper URL; identical copy on Robotopian). The AgileX download centre (https://global.agilex.ai/pages/download-manual) lists no PiPER files; AgileX GitHub has URDF/STL meshes (piper_ros) and DH parameters (piper_sdk) only. Arm-only STEP is in the rest/zero pose; arm+gripper STEP is in a different (extended) pose, so pose from the URDF (meshes in the link frames) or re-mate joints. Gripper stroke: the ORIGINAL/standard PiPER gripper (Nov-2024 manual, piper_ros URDF 2 x 35 mm prismatic, 'PiPER with Gripper' STEP measuring exactly 70.0 mm pad-to-pad, MGN7-145 rail) is 0-70 mm; AgileX's June-2025 manual and current resellers list a redesigned 0-100 mm gripper (shared with NERO), and the standalone 'AgileX_Gripper' STEP (internal name '100夹爪') is that 100 mm version. Check which one the lab owns. Base mounting: 4 x Ø5.4 through holes on 70 x 70 mm, pattern centre 5 mm behind the J1 axis (URDF x = +30 and -40, y = ±35). Also in the zip set but not downloaded: PiPER X arm (https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0673/6848/5000/files/AgileX_PiPERX_Robotic_Arm-1-STP.zip?v=1782225359).

ot2.notes: Official Opentrons reference model (SolidWorks 2016 export, 2018): 'OT-2 Reference Model Detailed.STEP' 3,943,530 B and 'OT-2 Reference Model Basic.STEP' 407,446 B, plus STLs, deck DXF and 5 window DXFs, from github.com/Opentrons/ot2 @ ef9ede1 (last commit 2018-05-09). Repo has no licence file; README grants use 'to modify their OT-2 robots however they choose'. STEP frame: X = width (centred), Y = up (0 = frame bottom, feet to -15), Z = depth (+Z = front/door). Door = two 5 mm panels (519.4 x 294.7 bottom, 519.4 x 261.42 top) stacked 54.55-612.17 mm above frame bottom with a 1.5 mm gap at ~350 mm (hinge line); the Opentrons spec sketch (SPECSOT2.png) shows a door panel swung outward and upward from that mid-height line. Hinge mechanics are not documented in the repo. Deck: 3 x 4 grid of 128 x 86 mm slots at 132.5 x 90.5 mm pitch; slot 12 = fixed trash.
